column3: At Ögedeiköl you will be asked who you know and who sent you, and the answers are checked.
What people at Ögedeiköl say about their safety is what they tell someone new; they may say more to someone they know.
The country around Ögedeiköl is thick with creatures and the town has answered it properly: there is a wall to hold and there are people to hold it, and both are in use constantly.

The walls and townsfolk of Ögedeiköl would see off a raid but not a proper army, and nothing now under way will change that. The supply book for Ögedeiköl's defenders runs short: the trades that should feed and equip them are failing, so the defence is weaker than its numbers suggest.
The town's law can name a wrong and cannot keep the person who did it, so it reaches for the purse or the road.
Trouble at Ögedeiköl has not turned into a collapse, because the town can pay its way through it.

There is a line around Ögedeiköl and it is kept: the gates shut, the works are repaired, and a stranger enters where the town intends him to. You come into Ögedeiköl by a gate, and someone at the gate sees you come.
There are people walking the town at Ögedeiköl at night, and the town's sense of itself rests more on that than on anything at the gate.
Ögedeiköl sends whoever it can against things they are not trained for, and pays for it each time.
Nothing unseen is known to have come at Ögedeiköl, but the town keeps no wards or seers that would notice if it had.
Ögedeiköl has not been attacked lately, and if it were, it would struggle to hold.
The guards at Ögedeiköl have changed their rounds and will not say why, and everyone can guess.
Ögedeiköl should come through this crisis if nothing else goes wrong, though its defence has had to change to meet it.
Nobody in Ögedeiköl thinks of the town walls as ornament; the town knows what it is for and checks it.
Ögedeiköl has a harbour and nothing to hold it with; any vessel that wants the sea approaches has them.
Ask at Ögedeiköl who runs things on the quiet and you get blank looks; either nobody does, or the town hides it very well.
The criminals at Ögedeiköl have bought their way into the hall, and each favour they get makes the next one easier.
